piece.dm_text:
Here is the n8n vs Zapier quick decision guide for your business workflows:

1. n8n Community Tier: Free self-hosted software (GitHub download). Full control, but you handle server updates, security, and backups.
2. n8n Cloud Starter: $20/month (billed annually) for ~2,500 executions/month and 5 concurrent runs.
3. n8n Cloud Pro: $50/month (billed annually) for 10,000 executions/month with role access controls.
4. n8n Business: $800/month (billed annually) for 40,000 executions; requires self-hosting with forum-only support.
5. Zapier: Managed cloud automation with ready integrations if you don't want server maintenance overhead.

[68] Zapier Blog — n8n pricing: Is it worth it?
URL: https://zapier.com/blog/n8n-pricing
When I got married, my mom and I visited countless bakeries looking for the perfect wedding cake. Nothing quite hit the mark. So she did what any completely rational mother of the bride would do: she made the cake herself. It ended up being perfectly customized to our specifications (raspberry dark chocolate with buttercream frosting)—but it also added more than a few gray hairs and kept her up until 2 a.m. the night before, hand-perfecting the icing.
n8n's pricing works a lot like that decision. You can go the completely free, fully DIY route with self-hosting and infinite flexibility, but you're also signing up for the infrastructure equivalent of staying up all night piping buttercream. Or you can pay for one of n8n's supported versions. One option gives you control; the other gives you convenience. And with n8n, neither is effortless.
In this guide, I'll dig into how n8n's pricing works, including cloud vs. self-hosting, and the real costs behind each. Then, we'll explore how it all stacks up against Zapier: the only bakery in this analogy where you can just walk in, choose what you need, and walk out with something baked to order and reliable enough for the real world—without anybody losing sleep in the process.
n8n (short for "nodemation") is a source-available automation tool that lets you build workflows using a visual, node-based editor. If you've used other automation builders, the general idea will feel familiar: you connect steps on a canvas to automate tasks across your apps and data. Where n8n differs is in how much customization it allows—especially if you're comfortable digging into technical details.
Because it offers a self-hosted version , many teams explore n8n as a potentially lower-cost option compared to managed automation platforms. In this scenario, you're responsible for setup, security, scaling, and maintenance. For some teams that already have the technical headcount to manage the infrastructure, that tradeoff keeps costs stable. For others, the extra overhead becomes its own kind of expense, even if it doesn't show up on an invoice.
Other teams (especially those related to the government or military) want a self-hosted option due to strict regulatory regimes or air-gapped security requirements. In those cases, the costs associated with self-hosting are a necessary evil.
n8n also offers a cloud-hosted version for people who don't want to manage the infrastructure themselves, but that comes with its own pricing structure (more on that later). In general, the tool is flexible and powerful, but it also assumes a level of technical comfort that not every business has the bandwidth for—something worth keeping in mind when comparing the total cost of using it long-term.
n8n comes in two versions, cloud and self-hosted—and the difference really comes down to who's responsible for keeping the lights on. With n8n's cloud subscription, everything is managed for you. You sign up, open the app, and start building. You don't have to think about servers, updates, uptime, or security patches, and the pricing is predictable because you're paying for a hosted service, not whatever your infrastructure happens to cost that month.
Self-hosting n8n flips that equation. You can download the free Community tier on GitHub, and you'll run it on your infrastructure—whether that's a VPS, Docker setup, or your own hardware. You get far more control: you can customize your environment, manage your own data storage, and build deeply tailored workflows that might not be possible in a managed setup. But with that freedom comes responsibility. You're the one handling updates, backups, monitoring, and anything that goes wrong at inconvenient times.
The higher-tier n8n plans can also be self-hosted (in fact, the Business tier requires that you self-host). Essentially, this means you're paying consumption-based pricing regardless of whether you're self-hosting or not. The Business tier also gets you admin and scaling features like SSO and LDAP, Git-based version control, and queue mode, even though n8n isn't hosting the software for you. Support is still forum-only, though. Dedicated support with an SLA is reserved for Enterprise.
So the choice is really about convenience versus control. If you want the simplest path to working automations, cloud hosting (on one of the lower tiers or a custom cloud Enterprise plan) gets you there faster with fewer moving parts. If you need full ownership of your environment or have strict privacy or customization requirements, self-hosting gives you the flexibility to shape n8n however you want—just with a lot more work (and hidden costs) on your plate.
If you decide to go with a managed setup, I'd argue you're better off going with Zapier instead because of the wider range of cloud subscription tiers, more pre-built integrations, and easier AI automation for your whole company.
Here are n8n's main pricing tiers and what comes with them. Pricing can change quickly, though, so visit the n8n pricing page to be sure it's up to date.
Starter ($20/month billed annually) : This is the entry-level cloud plan. You get roughly 2,500 workflow executions per month (with unlimited steps inside each workflow), unlimited users, and 5 concurrent workflow executions. (Note: n8n offers a free cloud trial with 1,000 executions.)
Pro plan ($50/month billed annually) : If you need more monthly usage, this is the next step up. With Pro, you get higher execution quotas (10,000 per month) and additional team-friendly features, like more shared projects, admin/role-based access controls, global variables, and longer execution logs.
Business ($800/month billed annually) : This plan is best for small and mid-sized companies who are ready to scale and have the budget to match. It comes with 40,000 workflow executions per month, along with SSO and LDAP, Git-based version control, queue mode, and access to the n8n community forum. Keep in mind that it still requires users to self-host the software, and support is forum-only.
Enterprise (pricing on request) : This tier provides custom capacity for organizations with heavy or unpredictable automation needs. That typically means a large execution volume, advanced security or compliance features, dedicated support, and more flexibility around how n8n is deployed or managed. Enterprise users have the option to self-host or use it on the cloud.
Community tier (not pictured): This version of self-hosted n8n is free, but it's unsupported and runs under n8n's Sustainable Use License, which limits use to internal business or non-commercial purposes.
n8n is most appealing for teams that want maximum control and have the technical depth to support it. That means developers or technically advanced teams who like the flexibility of hand-coded automation but don't want to maintain a pile of custom scripts.
